rules: Use this roadmap as the structural authority for graph shape, claimability, gates, leases, collisions and report reduction.
Reconcile its June recommended node with the current open-work master and MVP runner state before dispatch.
Only the orchestrator may mutate router state; worker agents return scoped handoffs or read-only reports.

format_decision.reason: The project has too many planning markdown files for reliable orchestration. This file captures versions, dependencies, gates, active work, and a rolling planning frontier as structured data for Roadmap Lens and PlanRuntime.

planning_model.intent: The roadmap must stay at least one useful step ahead of active execution. It is not a static snapshot and not an unbounded speculative graph.

tree_layers.meaning: Nodes that can be claimed or are currently running.
Nodes that are ready to promote when current execution finishes or blocks.
Likely next branches with enough metadata for planning, but not yet claimable.
Ideas, domain tracks, and research branches that remain visually connected but muted.

agents_must_not: promote speculative nodes to claimable work without policy approval
create infinite planning branches to avoid execution

frontier_rules: Every active leaf should have at least one prepared_next node unless it is intentionally terminal.
A prepared_next node must include role, scope, gates, expected evidence, and stop rules.
Frontier candidates may be broader, but must state the uncertainty that keeps them unclaimable.
When a node completes, PlanRuntime promotes the best prepared_next child and asks for frontier refresh.
When a node blocks, PlanRuntime creates or activates an unblocker/gate node instead of skipping ahead.
When two branches touch the same hot file or capability, PlanRuntime adds a collision edge and blocks parallel claims.
If the graph grows without execution progress, the heartbeat must stop and ask for pruning or priority confirmation.

critical_risks.risk: Planning becomes self-referential and agents keep expanding the tree instead of shipping.
critical_risks.mitigation: Limit frontier depth and require execution progress or explicit operator approval before broadening.

critical_risks.risk: Agents mutate the roadmap to make their own work look unblocked.
critical_risks.mitigation: Use append-only plan events and distinguish proposed, accepted, and committed graph state.

critical_risks.risk: Speculative future branches become visually indistinguishable from approved work.
critical_risks.mitigation: Render candidate/speculative nodes muted and make claimability a separate explicit field.

critical_risks.risk: Collision and gate data becomes decorative rather than enforced.
critical_risks.mitigation: PlanRuntime must use collision/gate edges in assignment and dispatch decisions.

tomorrow_parallel_start.goal: Start several agents in parallel without write collisions. Each agent reads a scoped slice, returns a structured report, and the PlanGraph reducer decides which reports become accepted events.
tomorrow_parallel_start.operator_intent: Today is roadmap shaping only. Tomorrow should begin with maximum safe parallelism and no direct file writes from worker agents until the report protocol and claimability are clear.

launch_sequence.name: orchestrator_bootstrap
launch_sequence.action: Load this roadmap, verify git status, identify current untracked roadmap files, and open a report-ingest queue.
launch_sequence.exit: Known worktree state and ready-to-dispatch read-only scout packets.

launch_sequence.name: parallel_read_only_scouts
launch_sequence.action: Dispatch read-only agents for roadmap inventory, runtime model audit, report schema design, Lens graph design, and gate/collision policy.
launch_sequence.exit: All scouts submit AgentReport payloads only.

launch_sequence.name: plan_graph_reduction
launch_sequence.action: Validate reports, reject unsafe/raw reports, reduce accepted reports into plan events and prepared_next nodes.
launch_sequence.exit: Claimable implementation slices are explicit and collision-aware.

launch_sequence.name: implementation_wave_decision
launch_sequence.action: Choose whether to start write-capable implementation or continue read-only refinement.

Read-only reports may propose nodes or events but cannot make nodes claimable without accepted reducer/orchestrator policy.

plan_event_model.reason: A mutating roadmap needs an audit trail. Current graph state should be derived from accepted events, not overwritten prose.

event_types.effect: Stores a redacted structured observation report as untrusted input.
Records that schema, scope, redaction, and source provenance passed validation.
Records why a report could not affect future context or plan state.
Allows derived plan events, gates, context summaries, or frontier proposals to be generated from the report.
Adds a candidate node that is not claimable yet.
Promotes a proposed node into the committed graph.
Moves a prepared node into current_execution when dependencies and gates allow it.
Creates or refreshes a lease for one agent.
Marks a node blocked and may propose an unblocker node.
Attaches pass, warn, block, fail, or skip evidence to a node or edge.
Adds a collision edge between nodes, files, capabilities, or agents.
Marks verified completion only after required evidence and gates pass.
Adds or updates prepared_next and frontier_candidates after progress.
Keeps a branch visible but removes claimability.

read_only_agent_report_pipeline.goal: Keep agents read-only at first. They inspect scoped context, then send a structured report to the PlanGraph. The PlanGraph validates, redacts, reduces, and only then updates future context.
future_context_rules: Future agents receive accepted report summaries and derived events, not raw report bodies by default.
Every context item must carry source_refs and confidence.
Rejected reports remain audit-only and must not be used as factual context.
Conflicting reports create a gate or blocker instead of silently choosing one.
A report may propose a next node, but cannot make that node claimable.
critical_limits: Read-only agents can still pollute context with confident but wrong summaries.
The PlanGraph reducer must preserve uncertainty instead of smoothing it away.
Reports must be compact; large raw notes, logs, provider output, and chat dumps are not valid context artifacts.

selection_order: Read current_execution nodes assigned to the agent role.
Filter out nodes with unsatisfied dependencies.
Filter out nodes with active collision, lock, or required gate blockers.
Prefer nodes with explicit ContextCapsule and focused tests.
After live-verified completion, select the next claimable node by dependency satisfaction, gate/collision/lock clearance, and priority_rank.
If no current node is claimable, inspect prepared_next and request promotion.
If prepared_next is empty for an active leaf, propose a frontier refresh instead of inventing work.
If multiple nodes are equally claimable and overlap risk is unclear, stop for orchestrator choice.
must_stop_when: the next node is not claimable
a required gate is block or fail
a file or capability collision exists
the agent lacks role, budget, lease, or workspace permission
the node would require live execution without operator Go
the agent would need to mutate the graph to make its own work valid

visual_rules: Show Now and 0.9 nodes as primary.
Show After 0.9 nodes behind the 0.9 milestone band.
Show Later/Research nodes muted and farther back.
Show current_execution, prepared_next, frontier_candidates, and speculative_backlog as separate visual layers inside each version band.
Highlight claimable nodes separately from candidate nodes.
Render collision edges as blocking edges, not decorative references.
Render gate nodes and stop conditions on the path an agent would traverse.
Warn when a markdown roadmap is newer than this JSON artifact.
Render done fake-runtime work as foundation, not as active work.
Show when a branch needs frontier refresh because no prepared_next node exists.
